statement: (i) Write down the general term in the expansion of $(1-x)^{-3}$ (for $|x|<1$). (ii) Hence show that the coefficient of $x^{n}$ is $\\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{2}$. (iii) Check your formula for $n=2$ and $n=5$.
solution: (i) $(1-x)^{-3}=\\sum_{r=0}^{\\infty}\\binom{r+2}{2}x^{r}$ since $\\binom{-3}{r}(-1)^{r}=\\binom{r+2}{2}$. (ii) Thus the coefficient of $x^{n}$ is $\\binom{n+2}{2}=\\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{2}$. (iii) For $n=2$: $3\\cdot4/2=6$ (matches $1+3x+6x^{2}+\\dots$); for $n=5$: $6\\cdot7/2=21$.
